course_name_original: Métodos Heurísticos para Planificación y Scheduling
course_name_en: Heuristic Methods for Planning and Scheduling
prerequisites: Estructuras Discretas y Análisis de Algoritmos

learning_outcomes.text: Understand planning and scheduling problems and their formalization as constrained combinatorial optimization problems.
Know how to apply heuristic search techniques, constraint propagation, and metaheuristics to these problems.
Understand the characteristics of planning and scheduling problems that arise in real situations, such as uncertainty or the dynamic nature of data, constraints, and objective functions.
Know and be able to use tools for solving planning problems and constraint optimization problems applicable to scheduling problems.
Know some real-world applications of planning and scheduling problems in areas such as transportation, energy efficiency, production management, system maintenance, etc.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to planning and scheduling problems. Definition and formalization.
Problem-solving techniques for optimization and constraint satisfaction: Heuristics, Constraint Programming, Metaheuristics and Hyperheuristics.
Real-world scenarios of optimization and constraint satisfaction problems.

assessment_methods.method: Reports / Memoranda / Practice Exams (P) - Genetic Programming Project (PG)
Reports / Memoranda / Practice Exams (P) - Genetic Algorithms Project (AG)
Reports / Memoranda / Practice Exams (P) - Constraint-Based Scheduling Project (PR)

assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as: 0.3 * ET + 0.03 * CP + 0.07 * CS + 0.25 * PG + 0.15 * AG + 0.15 * PR + A. For the CS component, it is mandatory to have completed and submitted the Scheduling practices deliverable on time. Attendance (A) is 0.05 if attendance >= 80%, and 0 if attendance < 80%. No minimum grade is established for any individual component. To pass, a minimum final score of 5 out of 10 points is required. In extraordinary calls, the assessment includes a Theoretical Exam (30%), a Presential Test on Planning and Scheduling (15%), and three practical projects (25%, 15%, 15%). To pass, a minimum final score of 5 out of 10 points is required in extraordinary calls. The teaching staff may require an oral defense of any assessable test or practical work.
